title.narrative: Agriculture Market Infrastructure Project (formerly Commercial Agriculture Development Project)

description.narrative:
The proposed Agriculture Market Infrastructure Project (the Project) will deliver the following key outputs: (i) improved agricultural marketing infrastructure and (ii) improved product standards and certification systems.
The Project will invest in the following livestock processing and horticultural market facilities: (i) two slaughterhouses in Kabul and three in the provinces; (ii) small-scale packing, sorting, grading, drying, and cold storage facilities in horticultural production areas; and (iii) laboratories for product certification.
Technical support will be provided in the areas of market infrastructure design, product standards, laboratory systems and certification, and produce marketing.
Ministry of Agriculture, Irrigation, and Livestock (MAIL) capacity will be strengthened in sanitary and phytosanitary policy and regulations, product standards, and agricultural aspects of accession to the World Trade Organization.

description.narrative: More efficient horticulture and livestock agribusiness industries

7% increase in domestic consumption of horticulture products by 2016 Progress/Status: 19 Farm Level Collection Centers (FLCC) have been constructed in 18 districts of Kabul, Balkh, Herat, Kunduz, Paktya, Kandahar and Nangarhar provinces. In 2016 7 FLCCs were handed over to cooperatives in Herat and Kandahar and one in Balk district and the remaining 12 FLCCs were handed over to a national firm (Agroindust) through a competitive process. Recently the government is considering to announce the FLCCs and reassigning to private sector on the basis of Public Partnership Law that was recently passed. In order to strengthen the capacity of the institutions for development of standards and regulations for improved product quality, which will support sector growth and agricultural trade a food safety grades and standards (FSGS) specialist was recruited under the Grant who prepared standards of grade for raisin and pomegranates. This will lead to greater value addition and improvement of the quality of the product processed and increased export of the horticulture products.
In addition, as per the scope of work, trainings of capacity building relevant to the operation and management of the FLCCs have also been provided to operators of the FLCC. During the Q2 2016 thirty MAIL/DAIL staff and two marketers of fruits and vegetables received training for Quality Management which included HACCP system development, Good Manufacturing Practices for FLCCs in three weeks. The training also included post-harvest management, supply chain management, and business administration. It is worth mentioning that these trained people will be providing training at province level to FLCC operators and will be supervising their day to day activities. Data Source: Government statistics, agribusiness surveys, and reports

Increased consumption of hygienically slaughtered meat in Kabul and major provincial cities by at least 15% by 2017 Progress/Status: It was anticipated that by March 2017 the construction works of the slaughterhouses (SH) and Public Privat Partnership (PPP) activities would be completed but due to unexpected delays during the implementation of the project, the said activities have not been completed. There were many delays during project implementation such as finalization of detailed design of the SHs, BRT issue, slow tax exemption, the late handover of sites (land) to Dogus Makina (DM), the contractor for SHs, security and financial and contract management problems of DM. After the technical evaluation of the SH contract and DM's request for additional financing, the technical team of MAIL came with a proposal to extend the contract of SH up to end of May 2018 and also it was found by the technical team that around 11 million additional funds were needed to rectify design deficiencies and cost overrun. To cover the financial gap, the government requested ADB to provide additional financing. ADB obtained a confirmation from the Department for International Development of the Government of United Kingdom (DFID) to provide $11.0 million for the project through ADB-administered Afghanistan Infrastructure Trust Fund (AITF). The proposed additional financing was for the government to complete the project's component 1, with the scope and scale as originally envisaged, and to enable the project to deliver the intended development outcomes. At the end of Sept 2015 the Board oard approved additional financing of $11 million.
A work plan for the PPP of the SH houses has been developed in close coordination and consultation with the Central PPP Unit and the Ministry of Finance. The concept paper and the feasibility study report for PPP of the SH which were produced by an international consultant in 2017 were approved by High Economic Council (HEC) of the government. The prequalification documents for PPP are prepared and the actual activities of PPP will take effect after successful completion and handover of the SH.
Despite the additional financing was provided to the SH contract in 2015, the implementation progress/status did not significantly change. DM was suffering from financial constraints which could not help the implementation status and such affected the project further. In order to cope with and get rid of this condition, MAIL assigned the remaining activities of the slaughter-houses in prior agreement with the contractor (DM) to a local financially capable firm. At the same time MAIL on 29 April 2017 submitted ADB a request for extending the contract until 30 May 2018, which was responded and no-objection was issued to extend the project until 30 June 2019. The new assignee for implementation of the contract is on board and has started the activities. Since the assignment of the SH activities, the performance on the SH sites has been changed positively. The SH in Reskhor, Kabul was inaugurated on 11 October 2018. the SH in Shakardara, Herat and Balkh provinces were completed in June 2019. Currently testing and commissiong of the SH equipment and handover of the SH are in progress. The SH in Kunduz will not be completed due to current security situation and the activities have been kept on hold until normality is restored in the province. MAIL has provided assurance to ADB through a letter to complete the remaining activities of the SH in Kunduz using their own resources. Data Source: Project monitoring system; Export Promotion Agency of Afghanistan reports Actual value:
